coaching.headline: A proper objective win. The duo still has work to do.
coaching.team: We took the early Fangtooths, Mini Prime and then the late major objectives, with Greystone leading our damage and Khaimera doing the heavy objective work. That is how a lead becomes a win instead of a fucking sightseeing tour. The weak spot was the duo: early deaths, then both dying before the enemy took Fangtooth. The finish was strong. That rough stretch still deserves attention.

focus.title: Agree on the exit before the fight
focus.action: Before the next objective setup, Drongo and Phase name the retreat route and whether Link pull is available. If the frontline backs out, both disengage together rather than taking a fresh trade.

perPlayer.3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a: Greystone put in a hell of a shift: our highest hero damage without a death. Keep that pressure and give the next objective setup the same presence. When Khaimera starts an objective, Greystone should hold the enemy approach and turn onto Kwang or Grux if they threaten Drongo. Being hard to kill is worth more when it buys the carry room to shoot.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Khaimera did the objective work this win needed. Keep that shit. Against Kwang, call the target before leaping and confirm who can follow; Tainted Guard punishes drawn-out basic-attack trades by cutting healing. If the backline is out of reach, hit the reachable threat with the team instead of turning a good objective setup into a solo expedition.
perPlayer.572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036: Gideon combined useful damage with very little downtime from deaths. Keep the patient spell pressure. When Grux or Kwang can still interrupt Black Hole, wait for their control to be spent or for a protected angle before committing. Truesilver helps while its shield holds; it is not a fucking permission slip to channel wherever looks exciting.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: The win does not erase Drongo's rough game: damage below his usual and more deaths, with Kwang repeatedly collecting the kill. Keep contributing to objectives, but make safe firing time the priority. When Kwang is unaccounted for, hold Pacifier for separation; once he commits into the frontline, build Rad Rounds on the nearest safe target instead of reaching past it for Skylar.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Phase's healing and vision work mattered. The early deaths were still a bloody expensive start, and more wards are not the whole answer. Against Argus and Kwang, stay offset from Drongo so the same engage cannot easily catch both. If Drongo needs pulling out, do it before the immobilize lands: Link cannot rescue an already immobilized ally. Keep the support output, improve the escape setup.

12.call: The team collected kills across this sequence and secured Fangtooth. Preserve that conversion: once the nearby threat is gone, name the objective and send the healthy players who can safely reach it. These credits do not establish a single five-on-five fight.

17.7.call: We collected kills while an Outer Tower fell in the same window. Before continuing the chase, check whether a threatened wave needs clearing or whether the team can take something worth more. The record does not identify who could have reached that tower.

19.6.call: Phase and Drongo died before their Fangtooth; our kills in the same window did not prevent it. With the duo down, call whether the pit is genuinely contestable. If it is not, trade a safe available resource and regroup instead of sending more bodies into an uncertain contest.

matchup: Kwang adds a tether and knockup threat, and Link cannot pull an immobilized ally.
Rescue timing matters more than simply stacking healing.
build: Tainted Scepter has real targets in Skylar's Terminus, Kwang's omnivamp and Grux's healing.
Prophecy is a damage choice rather than protection; the inventory does not show how often Blighted Spells landed.
eternal: Immaculate is a defensive draft alternative to Prima Donna, trading damage for mitigation near full health.
The early deaths alone do not prove Prima Donna caused them.
augment: The record does not show who was linked or whether mana was ever short for Psychic Support.
Kindred Surge is a more direct escape and sustain tool for the duo once Hyperflux is online.
crest: Tranquility fits the job: a group heal with brief mitigation, plus a third ward slot.
Phase placed more wards than her usual on the hero.
improvement: If Drongo keeps getting locked down within Phase's reach, Enra's Blessing over Prophecy is the most relevant comparison.
Keep Tainted Scepter if Phase can reliably apply it to the enemy healing targets.
A protection-versus-damage decision, not a penalty for buying off-meta.

matchup: Zinx was the enemy's top hero damage dealer; burst her after Neural Regenesis is spent.
Grux and Kwang are the divers who can reach Gideon during Black Hole's channel.
build: Truesilver Bracelet's shield has a clear purpose against Grux and Kwang during Black Hole.
It does not make the channel safe after the shield breaks.
eternal: Mind Rot is the more offensive draft alternative, giving up Phylactery's protection and cooldown benefit.
augment: Infinite Impact pairs neatly with Soulbinder for a long-range poke plan.
Event Horizon is the alternative into the Grux and Kwang health pools, traded for the cross-map Void Breach.
crest: Obelisk suits a mid who gets takedowns, but it is pure damage with no escape or protection.
improvement: Keep Truesilver as the interruption safeguard in this matchup.
If Zinx or Argus damage becomes the problem, compare a magical-defense slot against Oblivion Crown; this match does not establish that need.

matchup: Kwang and Skylar were both repeatedly credited with killing Drongo.
Kwang's Tainted Guard bleeds and cuts Drongo's healing when he attacks Kwang; Skylar brings lifesteal and an execute.
build: A coherent damage plan, but it still needs time in basic-attack range.
More finishing damage is not automatically the fix for lower damage and elevated deaths.
eternal: This setup rewards converting an opening into sustained shots.
Natural Resistance is a defensive draft alternative to Forage, trading income for a cleanse; not a reason to accept an avoidable engage.
augment: Shred Spree brings the 30% armor shred up far more often, at half damage.
With four of our five heroes dealing physical damage, more shred on Kwang and Grux helps the whole team.
crest: Pacifier can create separation from Kwang or help finish; chase the reset only if the next position is safe.
The deaths do not establish misuse; compare a defensive crest only if control, not damage, stops Drongo firing.
improvement: Do not automatically replace Imperator with Tainted Rounds: Phase and Greystone already bring healing reduction.
If Drongo must fight Skylar or Kwang without that coverage, Tainted Rounds applies it himself, giving up critical damage.
Team coverage and reachable targets decide this, not a popular core.

matchup: Grux's healing makes anti-heal relevant, and he finished with the most deaths in the lobby.
Zinx was their top hero damage dealer, with Argus adding magical damage.
build: This supports brawling with Grux; Tainted Blade addresses his healing.
Zinx and Argus remain reasons to watch magical damage.
eternal: Keep the combination: it fits Greystone's extended fights better than choosing from the damage chart alone.
augment: Imperial Soul fits a frontline landing the ultimate on several enemies at once.
Tainted Oath is the anti-heal alternative, but Tainted Blade already covers that job.
crest: Razorback is a sensible defensive crest into Grux's stuns and Kwang's knockup.
improvement: No forced swap from this game; zero deaths supports keeping what worked.
If Zinx or Argus end Greystone's frontline time, Absolution over Giant's Ring trades health and physical armor for magical armor and tenacity.

matchup: Kwang's Tainted Guard and Argus's Tainted Scepter are two direct answers to Khaimera's regeneration-based sustain.
Khaimera's kills were spread across Kwang, Zinx, Grux and Argus.
build: Ashbringer, Claw of Hermes and Nuclear Rounds have synergy to investigate.
Final totals cannot isolate their value from target access or objective availability.
eternal: Exarch works on self-healing, so it fits Khaimera; keep it as a coherent choice.
Enemy healing reduction pressures the sustain but does not prove the Exarch buff was disabled.
augment: Jungle Invasion rewards a jungler who invades and fights on their side of the map.
Nothing in this match makes a clear case for Feral Ambush or Lane Lurker over it.
crest: Judgement stacks with regeneration and Fervour into a sustain package.
The same enemy anti-heal applies to it.
improvement: Do not replace this build merely because it differs from the popular core.
If Kwang and Argus cut fights short, compare Absolution against Nuclear Rounds, sacrificing ability amplification and some attack speed.
If Khaimera can already stay on targets, retain the offensive package.

threats: Chain-CC risk (2 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s), Kwang Surge of the Heavens (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Our damage is 4/5 physical — predictable; the enemy itemizes one armor item against most of it. A magical pick would split their defenses.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

Stack (Kept alive in fights): 5 effects on one trigger: Aegis Of Agawar, Razorback, Nihil, From the Abyss, Adaptive Plating. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 2 effects on one trigger: Augmentation, Giant's Ring.
The Eternal was part of it: Nihil (From the Abyss + Adaptive Plating) sits on the same trigger as the items (kept alive in fights), so every extra second in a fight made them harder to kill.
Countered? 2 of the 4 players Greystone killed built physical armor (Argus, Kwang). We killed Greystone 0 times.
Copy it? Nihil (From the Abyss + Adaptive Plating): 55.8% in 423 Greystone offlane games, above the hero's 51.7%. Proven this patch: worth copying.

worked.eternalPart: The Eternal was part of it: Nihil (From the Abyss + Adaptive Plating) sits on the same trigger as the items (kept alive in fights), so every extra second in a fight made them harder to kill.

countered.text: 2 of the 4 players Greystone killed built physical armor (Argus, Kwang).

copy.text: Nihil (From the Abyss + Adaptive Plating): 55.8% in 423 Greystone offlane games, above the hero's 51.7%. Proven this patch: worth copying.

loadout.name: Imperial Soul
loadout.text: Stone Forged Soul deals 12% more damage and its radius is 20% larger.

ability.name: Stone Forged Soul
ability.what: Greystone enters Stasis for 2.5s, restoring 14/16/18% (+2.5%) of his maximum health (increased by up to 2.5x based on missing health) and Slowing nearby Enemies by up to 70%, based on proximity.

loadout.plain: Stone Forged Soul hits harder in a bigger area. Use it in the middle of the enemy team to slow and crush as many as possible.

loadout.name: Nihil
loadout.text: Damage a hero to gain Doom for 3s. Doom grants 1 Physical Power, 2 Magical Power, 1 Physical Armor & 1 Magical Armor for every 3s it persists. On level-up or Takedown, the stats Doom grants are permanently increased by 20%.
loadout.plain: Staying in fights with heroes builds up power and armor over time, and level-ups or takedowns make it permanently stronger. Fits Greystone's long duels.

loadout.name: From the Abyss
loadout.text: Restore 0.2/0.4/0.7/1% Max Health/s (Levels 1/6/11/16) while in Hero Combat or out of enemy vision.
loadout.plain: Heals a share of your max health every second while fighting heroes or hidden, on top of your passive regen.

loadout.name: Adaptive Plating
loadout.text: Taking damage grants matching Armor (1% per hit, stacks 10x).
loadout.plain: Getting hit gives you armor of the matching type. Helps Greystone soak damage when he leaps into the enemy team.

loadout.name: Razorback
loadout.text: Echidna:  Gain 20% Physical Armor and Magical Armor for 5s. Reflect 15% of Pre-Mitigated Damage received from Heroes as Damage.
loadout.plain: Briefly more armor, and part of the damage heroes deal to you hits them back. Pop it when the enemy team focuses you after Assault The Gates.

lead.title: Hard to kill
lead.text: Never died in 25 minutes, fewer deaths than about 95% of Greystone offlane players this patch. The build added health and armor. It came from the Eternal setup (Nihil, From the Abyss, Adaptive Plating) plus Razorback, Aegis Of Agawar.
